name: PASH Syndrome (Pyoderma Gangrenosum, Acne, and Suppurative Hidradenitis Syndrome)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis based on triad presentation

criteria.description: Presence of pyoderma gangrenosum lesions characterized by painful, necrotic ulcers with violaceous borders
Chronic, recurrent, painful nodules and abscesses in apocrine gland-bearing areas consistent with hidradenitis suppurativa
Severe nodulocystic acne typically involving the face, chest, or back
Exclusion of other autoinflammatory syndromes such as PAPA or PAPASH

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: pyoderma gangrenosum, hidradenitis suppurativa, and severe nodulocystic acne
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may support but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pyoderma gangrenosum ulcers with violaceous undermined borders
searchTerms: painful skin ulcers with purple edges

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent painful nodules and abscesses in apocrine gland-bearing regions
searchTerms: recurrent painful skin nodules and abscesses
repeated boils in sweat gland areas
chronic painful skin lumps in armpits or groin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe nodulocystic acne affecting face, chest, or back
searchTerms: severe cystic acne on face and body
nodulocystic acne on chest or back
deep acne with nodules and cysts

common.symptomName: Chronic draining sinus tracts in affected skin areas
Pain and tenderness localized to skin lesions
Erythema and swelling surrounding nodules and ulcers
searchTerms: swelling and redness near skin bumps

common.symptomName: Low-grade fever during active inflammatory episodes
searchTerms: slight temperature increase in active disease

occasional.symptomName: Arthralgia or arthritis affecting peripheral joints
searchTerms: joint pain in hands and feet
excessive sweating in affected skin areas

occasional.symptomName: Scarring and keloid formation at lesion sites

rare.symptomName: Ocular inflammation such as episcleritis or uveitis

searchTerms: tender lymph nodes close to affected skin

laboratory: Neutrophilic dermal infiltrates on skin biopsy
Negative bacterial cultures from sterile ulcers
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing abscesses and sinus tracts in hidradenitis suppurativa lesions
other: Histopathology showing neutrophilic dermatosis without vasculitis

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations in PSTPIP1 more common
Includes pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, acne, and hidradenitis suppurativa
Genetic overlap but distinct clinical presentation

redFlags: Rapid progression of necrotic skin ulcers
Systemic symptoms such as high fever or malaise
Development of secondary bacterial infections in skin lesions
references: Marzano AV, et al. PASH syndrome: a rare autoinflammatory disorder. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2017.
Wolfe CM, et al. Clinical and genetic features of PASH syndrome. Dermatology. 2020.
